title: West Berkshire Council: Development of generative AI tools
summary: West Berkshire reports faster, more consistently formatted job adverts from its GPT tool, with low stated setup and running costs.
account: West Berkshire used GPT-based tools to generate job advertisements and explored internal and public-information assistants. Managers report less drafting time and more consistent formatting. The source reports roughly £300 in setup staff time and £2 in monthly running costs. Recycling and policy assistants were planned, and their benefits had not been established.
purpose: Reduce work drafting recruitment material and explore customized assistants for council information.
system: Custom job-advert generator using OpenAI GPT models and the ChatGPT API; other assistant prototypes
developer: West Berkshire Council using OpenAI models

ratings.reason: The implemented job-advert tool saves drafting time and standardizes presentation. These are modest workflow gains.
Managers report less time drafting postings. No applicant or employment outcome is inferred.

ai_role.statement: The deployed tool converts structured job information into draft advertisements and related content. Managers report shorter drafting time and consistent formatting. Other information assistants remain in development or testing.

evidence.citation: Local Government Association, AI case-study bank. Council or project account published by LGA. Hosting and editorial curation do not establish independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: West Berkshire Council: Development of generative AI tools

produced_by: Forms collect job details and feed them to the OpenAI API through the council’s existing digital platform.
Manager feedback informed evaluation of generated content.
must_hold: The source does not establish which conditions are necessary to reproduce the reported benefit.
